title.zh: 分子氢质子弹性动量转移截面

summary: H2-on-H+ elastic momentum-transfer cross section in m^2 as a function of collision energy in eV: a single five-coefficient logarithmic polynomial on the clipped [0.03, 1.01e4] eV domain. Negative energies are rejected.

capability: H2-on-H+ elastic momentum-transfer cross section in m^2 from collision energy in eV.
operation: Evaluate the H2-on-H+ elastic momentum-transfer cross section
collision energies -> cross section per energy
discovery.model: Single declared five-coefficient logarithmic-polynomial fit; no external-data interpolation and no rate integration.
discovery.geometry: None; scalar material function of collision energy with no spatial axis (coordinate: collision energy in eV; output in m^2).
discovery.boundary: Energies must be finite and nonnegative; values outside the [0.03, 1.01e4] eV fit range clip to the endpoints.

identity.relation: the H2-on-H+ elastic momentum-transfer cross section as a function of collision energy
identity.direction: collision energies -> cross section per energy
identity.definition: Energies are clipped to [0.03, 1.01e4] eV and the cross section is exp(polyval(log(E_clipped), a)) * 1e-4 m^2 with the five coefficients. Endpoint values repeat outside the clipped range; values above the upper edge emit ApplicabilityWarning.
identity.model: a single declared cross-section fit; no interpolation of external data and no rate integration
identity.geometry: none; a scalar material function of collision energy
identity.coordinates: collision energy in eV; output cross section in m^2
identity.boundary: energies must be finite and nonnegative; in-domain values outside the fit range clip to the range endpoints
assumptions: The coefficients are the declared fit values, evaluated with the declared expression; they are not re-derived from any external reference.
No external physical cross-section reference is bound; this residual stays open.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: Collision energies at which the cross section is evaluated.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative. Values below the fit range are clipped silently; values above it are clipped to the upper endpoint and emit ApplicabilityWarning.

outputs.name: cross_section_m2
outputs.description: Elastic momentum-transfer cross section, one value per energy.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive for every accepted input.

preconditions: The caller accepts the clipping convention: energies outside the fit range return the endpoint value, with ApplicabilityWarning above the upper edge.
supported: H2-on-H+ elastic momentum-transfer cross sections on the fit within (or clamped to) its declared energy range.
Scalar and array evaluation of any shape, including zero-dimensional inputs.
excluded: Maxwellian averaging of this cross section: use scirel.collisions.maxwellian-relative-speed-rate-average, which accepts this callable as its cross_section_m2 port.
Charge-exchange or ionization channels: different relations, provided by sibling assets.
Elastic cross sections for other species pairs: separate assets, not variants of this relation.
A cross-section model validated against an external atomic-physics reference; none is bound.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError naming energy_ev for non-real, non-finite or negative energy inputs. There is no other failure mode.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Not reachable on the declared domain: the fit is evaluated only on its clipped positive range. Above 1.01e4 eV the call emits ApplicabilityWarning and returns the upper-endpoint value, which stays finite and strictly positive. No iteration, no state and no partial results.

example.description: Evaluate the fit on a grid, confirm the endpoint clipping, and confirm the negative-energy rejection.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_hydrogen2_proton_elastic_cross_section

energy = np.array([0.03, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0, 1.0e3, 1.01e4])
result = evaluate_hydrogen2_proton_elastic_cross_section(energy)
assert result.shape == energy.shape
assert np.all(np.isfinite(result)) and np.all(result > 0.0)
clipped = evaluate_hydrogen2_proton_elastic_cross_section(np.array([0.01, 0.03, 2.0e4, 1.01e4]))
assert clipped[0] == clipped[1] and clipped[-1] == clipped[-2]
try:
    evaluate_hydrogen2_proton_elastic_cross_section(np.array([1.0, -0.5]))
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'nonnegative' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('a negative energy must be rejected')
example.expected: Finite strictly positive cross sections in m^2; endpoint repetition outside the clipped range; ValueError naming nonnegativity for a negative energy.

scope: That the fit equals an independent evaluation of the coefficient set on the clipped domain to a relative tolerance of 1e-15, on in-domain and holdout grids.
The endpoint clipping: values below and above the fit range repeat the endpoint values exactly.
The input contract: non-finite and negative energies are rejected with messages naming the quantity; a negative energy raises rather than being silently clipped.

No external implementation comparison is maintained or replayed by this repository; the maintained tests validate the declared relation against an in-repository independent formulation and cover the stated rejection and clipping behaviour only on their tested grids.

Structural evidence: the returned value is the frozen fit re-evaluated on another code path and multiplied by the exact 1e-4 cm^2->m^2 factor (agreement within four binary64 roundings), the single clipped fit is the declared polynomial on its whole interval, the 1.01e4 eV edge repeats the endpoint with ApplicabilityWarning, and the measured log-slope equals the analytic derivative; this establishes structure, not an absolute table value, because the published table the coefficients were regressed from is not reachable from this repository

Precision budget: the unit-factor comparison admits 8e-16 relative, four binary64 roundings between two evaluation orders of the same polynomial; the slope identity admits 1e-4 of max(1, |d ln sigma / d ln E|) measured by a central difference of h = 1e-3 in ln E, whose truncation term h^2/6 |d^3 ln sigma / d(ln E)^3| stays below 1e-6 on the declared intervals; no existing per-asset tolerance is loosened and no numeric value is changed

Failure matrix: each `failure_semantics` channel of this contract has exactly one executable assertion in tests/collisions/test_declared_failure_channels.py; that table's channel set is compared with the exception and warning classes this contract names, and every callable must produce its declared class, so a channel cannot be added, renamed or dropped silently
verification.evidence_ceiling: An independent evaluation of the fit expressions covers every branch, clipping boundary and SI conversion; a NumPy-only installation passed scalar independent evaluation across 56 energies per branch, and all 62 fit/input tests passed with their original assertions and tolerances. This qualifies the stated empirical expression, not new experimental accuracy. No external experimental cross-section validation is bound, and redistribution permission remains separate.
known_limitations: The integrated input check rejects complex, boolean and numeric-string energies before float conversion; no coercion is performed. Valid real-input fit arithmetic is unchanged.
Neither branch is validated against an external atomic-physics reference; no external validation gap is closed here.
Energies outside the fit range return the endpoint value; values above the upper edge emit ApplicabilityWarning. This remains the declared clipping convention, not an error.
The negative-energy rejection is an explicit precondition of this contract: a negative energy raises ValueError rather than returning the clipped endpoint.
No environment-gated external-implementation comparison exists in this repository; any earlier external comparison is not replayed by the maintained tests.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.

Cannot establish: the absolute table values of this relation. They need the Janev (1995) chapter 11 H2-on-H+ momentum-transfer fit table, which are not in this repository and not available from a free source, so only the structural properties listed above are established; no coefficient or absolute cross section is asserted against a published number, and none was reconstructed from memory
